channel.title: Open Calls for Artists — Monographica
channel.description: Curated list of open calls for photographers and visual artists. Exhibitions, grants, residencies, and publications worldwide.

item.title: Sonntag Grant 2026 Photobook Open Call
item.description: Photobook open call from the Berlin-based Sonntag Grant for Photography in collaboration with Replika Publishing. Reserved for FLINTA artists (female, lesbian, inter, non-binary, trans, agender), 18+, of any nationality or location. Seeks projects that challenge the boundaries of the book as form, with emphasis on conceptual depth, material inquiry, and artistic dialogue. All forms of photographic work accepted; projects must be completed or at an advanced stage suitable for photobook production. AI-generated images are not accepted. One artist is selected to work directly with Replika Publishing to produce a new photobook with a print run of at least 350 copies (50 going to the artist). Submissions accepted globally from April 1 through midnight (Berlin/CET) on May 31, 2026. — Deadline: May 31, 2026. Fee: €10. Prize: Photobook publication (350+ copies).

item.title: Ucross Spring 2027 Residency
item.description: Two- to six-week residency at the Ucross Foundation's 20,000-acre working ranch in northeastern Wyoming. Spring Session 2027 runs February through early June. Open to visual artists, writers, composers, choreographers, interdisciplinary artists, performance artists, and collaborative teams; both established and emerging artists encouraged, international applicants welcome. Approximately 115 residents per year; up to 10 in residence at any time. Includes living accommodations, all meals (chef-prepared lunch and dinner Monday–Friday, plus weekend provisions), dedicated work space, weekly housekeeping, linens and towels, and wireless internet. No stipend; residents provide their own materials and arrange travel to Sheridan, WY. Application opens May 1, 2026; no fee waivers available. — Deadline: July 15, 2026. Fee: $40. Prize: 2–6 week residency.

item.title: SCAN Full Contact 2026
item.description: First edition of Full Contact, a professional photography meeting organised by SCAN, the international photography festival hosted by Tarragona City Council. Twelve photographers are selected for a portfolio-review and networking day at Teatret del Port in El Serrallo (Tarragona) on 17 October 2026, with accommodation, meals, and curatorial conversations covered. One project is selected as the Full Contact Award winner and receives a solo exhibition during SCAN's 2027 official programme along with a €900 fee (incl. tax) for exhibition and communication rights. Open to photographers of legal age residing in any country of the European Union or the United Kingdom. — Deadline: May 10, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: 2027 solo exhibition + €900.

item.title: Camera Work: Shadow and Light 2026 · Black Box Gallery
item.description: Juried photography exhibition at Black Box Gallery in Portland, Oregon, exploring the dialogue between shadow and light. Both black-and-white and color work welcome — formal, conceptual, expressive, minimal, intricate, literal, or abstract approaches all considered. Juried by Todd Johnson, gallery founder/director, with an MFA in Photography from the San Francisco Art Institute and 25 years in arts education and administration. 26 photographs selected for the physical exhibition (June 1–25, 2026); 50 additional images included in the online gallery; all 76 published in a purchasable catalog. Black Box provides free archival printing, matting, and framing for accepted work. The gallery retains 50% commission on sales. Open worldwide to amateur and professional photographers; submission via PayPal payment + email with up to 5 JPEGs. — Deadline: May 8, 2026. Fee: $40. Prize: Gallery exhibition + free printing/framing.

item.title: 2nd Street Photo Festival 2026
item.description: International street photography open call for the 2nd edition, hosted at the Athens School of Fine Arts. Submit 1–3 high-resolution photographs (minimum 4000 px on the long side, JPG or TIFF) via WeTransfer or cloud service to contest@streetphotofestival.gr, accompanied by a Word document with contact info, country, Instagram and website. Selected photographers contribute €50 toward festival expenses. Selected works exhibited at Athens School of Fine Arts December 12–20, 2026. All selected photographers receive a Certificate of Participation and Achievement. — Deadline: May 31, 2026. Fee: Free (€50 if selected). Prize: €400 + €300 + €200.

item.title: The Midnight Garden · Visionary Art Collective
item.description: Four-day NYC pop-up exhibition curated by Jessica Libor (founder/director of Era Contemporary). Theme centers on cultivation, transformation, and unseen processes of growth — both in nature and within ourselves — exploring blooming, decay, renewal, and the balance between control and wildness. Open to U.S.-based visual artists in all 2D and 3D media including photography. Exhibition August 20–23, 2026 at 61 Atlantic Ave, Brooklyn. Selected artists featured in New Visionary Magazine and listed on Artsy through Warnes Contemporary gallery. — Deadline: May 31, 2026. Fee: $25–35. Prize: Pop-up exhibition + magazine feature.

item.title: Rotlicht Festival 2026 — Anthropocene: Hybrid Realities
item.description: International open call from the Rotlicht Festival for Analog Photography in Vienna. Theme: Anthropocene: Hybrid Realities — submissions engaging with the tensions of the human-shaped epoch through experimental, critical, and process-oriented approaches in analog and hybrid photography. Purely digital work is excluded; at least one analog process must be involved. Open to anyone aged 16+ not affiliated with the festival. Photos must be from the last 5 years (2021–2026). Submit a single series or project (max 15 images). 20 winners are exhibited at the Academy of Fine Arts Vienna, each receiving a €250 honorarium, €150 travel allowance, festival pass, and inclusion in the official catalogue. The Grand Prix winner receives an additional solo exhibition, €250, and festival cover feature. Winners announced beginning of September 2026. — Deadline: June 30, 2026. Fee: €20. Prize: €250 + exhibition.

item.title: AAP Magazine #58 Black & White · All About Photo
item.description: Black & white theme issue of AAP Magazine. Open to photographers 18+; submit a cohesive series of at least 3 images (up to 40). 25 winners published in AAP Magazine Volume 58 with online gallery placement and a free copy. Cash prizes: $500 (1st), $300 (2nd), $200 (3rd). Early-bird fee ($30 for first 3 images, $5 each additional) ends May 15, 2026; regular fee $35 thereafter. Winners announced approximately July 15, 2026. — Deadline: June 2, 2026. Fee: $30–$35. Prize: $1,000 + publication.

item.title: Prairie Ronde Artist Residency — Fall 2026
item.description: Five- to six-week residency at The Mill in Vicksburg, Michigan — a 416,000-square-foot former paper mill on 80 acres of land. Fall session runs September 15 to December 20, 2026. Open to artists across all media including photography; the program does not limit residency to any specific medium and seeks artists who can engage directly with The Mill and its surrounding rural property. Two to four residents per session. Includes a $2,000 stipend on completion, $500 travel grant, private housing in a historic village home, gallery exhibition in downtown Vicksburg, video documentation, and brewery membership. Process-based residency for independently driven artists; one piece produced during the residency is donated to the permanent collection. International applicants are temporarily not being considered (as of April 2025). Selections announced July 30. — Deadline: June 15, 2026. Fee: $25. Prize: $2,000 stipend + gallery exhibition.

item.title: Transforming Landscapes — 20/20 Photo Festival 2026
item.description: International juried exhibition for analog photographers exploring how American landscapes have evolved over 250 years — physical, technological, societal, political, scientific, and artistic. Open exclusively to work made with analog photographic methods including film types (color negative, black-and-white, slide, instant) and formats (35mm, 120, 4×5 large format, 110, 126). Selected works exhibited at Cherry Street Pier during the 20/20 Photo Festival in Philadelphia, September 10–13, 2026. Juried by photographer Andrew Piccone. — Deadline: June 1, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: $500 + $250 + $150.

item.title: Lens Work: Trees and Water · Black Box Gallery
item.description: Juried group exhibition exploring trees and water as subjects in contemporary photography — dynamic and diverse imagery, including 'magical and poetic pictures' celebrating visual composition and contemporary photographic technique. Selected work shown in physical gallery and online annex; included in printed catalog. Free printing, matting, and framing for accepted artists. 50/50 sales commission. Exhibition August 1–25, 2026 in Portland, OR. Juror: Todd Johnson, Black Box Gallery founder. Open worldwide to amateur and professional photographers. — Deadline: July 10, 2026. Fee: $40. Prize: Exhibition + free framing.

item.title: UNSTAGED Journal — Instant Photography
item.description: Themed issue of UNSTAGED, an independent photography journal dedicated to lens-based inquiries into comforting and discomforting authenticity. Guest curated by Dani (@d.m.terblanche), this call invites personal stories told through instant photography (Polaroid, Instax, etc.) — focused on everyday moments rather than perfection. Tagline: 'You don't have to be good.' Submissions can include single images, diptychs, triptychs, or mixed-media approaches; lens-based instant photography only. Submit 5–10 photographs as JPG files (long edge 2000px, 300 DPI) with a project description (max 500 words). Upload work to a public Google Drive and send the link (with description as PDF) to reach@arek-ratai.com. Name files Name_ProjectTitle_01. Emails with attachments will be deleted. Free entry, free print publication for selected photographers. — Deadline: May 20, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Publication (print).

item.title: Photography+ Emerging Talent 2026 · Photoworks
item.description: International open call from Photography+, Photoworks' digital platform exploring how photography intersects with everyday life. Open to BA and MA graduates and image-based artists within their first five years of practice or graduation. 10 awardees featured in Photography+ online magazine and showcased in an evening projection at Kranj Foto Fest. One artist receives a year-long Photoworks membership plus curatorial and editorial mentoring; another receives a £200 Spectrum Photographic printing voucher and an Instagram takeover. Submit up to 15 images from a single project with a statement of up to 200 words. — Deadline: June 15, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: £200 voucher + Publication.

item.title: Source Graduate Photography Online 2026 — BA
item.description: Annual graduate showcase from Source, Belfast-based quarterly photography magazine, running since 2007. Open to photographers graduating from a BA in 2026 in Ireland or the UK. Submit up to 8 images with an artist statement and website link. Selected work featured on the Graduate Photography Online platform and in a printed supplement; participants receive a 1-year digital subscription to Source (worth £26.99). MA/MFA submissions have a separate later deadline (August 7, 2026). — Deadline: May 11, 2026. Fee: £33 / €38. Prize: Online exhibition + publication.

item.title: Source Graduate Photography Online 2026 — MA/MFA
item.description: Annual graduate showcase from Source, Belfast-based quarterly photography magazine, running since 2007. Open to photographers graduating from an MA or MFA in 2026 in Ireland or the UK. Submit up to 8 images with an artist statement and website link. Selected work featured on the Graduate Photography Online platform and in a printed supplement; participants receive a 1-year digital subscription to Source (worth £26.99). BA submissions have an earlier deadline (May 11, 2026). — Deadline: August 7, 2026. Fee: £33 / €38. Prize: Online exhibition + publication.

item.title: No-Type Monograph No. 01
item.description: Open call from No-Type, an independent Chicago photography publisher, for the inaugural artist monograph. The selected photographer receives a fully-funded monograph dedicated entirely to their work — editing, design, printing, and marketing all covered, plus 20% of the printed edition. A shortlist of six artists will be interviewed on No-Type's website, and all applicants are considered for inclusion in an Editor's Choice issue of the magazine. Open to lens-based projects of any subject, genre, or process; submissions must be a cohesive body of work ready for book form. — Deadline: May 31, 2026. Fee: $20. Prize: Publication.

item.title: Photo Shoot 2026 · Black Box Gallery
item.description: Open call from Black Box Gallery in Portland, OR. 26 photographs selected for in-gallery exhibition (July 1–25, 2026); 50 additional photographs included in an online gallery annex. All 76 selected works featured in a printed Blurb catalog. Free printing, matting, and framing for selected works. 50% commission to gallery on sales. Open to amateur and professional photographers worldwide. Juried by Todd Johnson (founder/director of Black Box Gallery, MFA San Francisco Art Institute). — Deadline: June 12, 2026. Fee: $40 for 5 images. Prize: Exhibition + free printing/framing.

item.title: SCAN Tarragona — Full Contact Award 2026 · SCAN International Photography Festival
item.description: Open call from SCAN, the international photography festival organized by Tarragona City Council. 12 projects selected for Full Contact, a professional meeting space at Teatret del Port in El Serrallo, Tarragona on October 17, 2026. From these 12, one artist receives the Full Contact Award: a solo exhibition in 2027 as part of SCAN's official program plus €900 fee for exhibition and communication rights. Open to EU and UK residents of legal age. Submit any photo series that tells a story, on any subject. Maximum 16 photographs from a single series. — Deadline: May 10, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Solo exhibition + €900.

item.title: Photoworks Guest Issue 4 — Rituals
item.description: Fourth edition of Photoworks Guest, a community photo zine published by Photoworks SF in San Francisco. Theme: Rituals — exploring the relationship between rituals and photography. Examples include daily commutes, ceremonies, holiday traditions, cooking, or anything you do every day. Selected work appears in the print magazine; longer features with interviews are also available for projects that fit the theme. — Deadline: May 15, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Publication (print).

item.title: Łódź Photo-Match 2026 Portfolio Review · Fotofestiwal
item.description: Two-day portfolio review at Fotofestiwal in Łódź, June 19–20, 2026. Twenty selected photographers each get up to four one-on-one meetings with European curators, editors, and gallery directors based on a matching process. Day 1 features public presentations; Day 2 holds private reviews at Alfred Biedermann's Palace. Open internationally, including artistic duos. Physical attendance required. Reviewers from Spain, Italy, Lithuania, Poland, UK, Finland, Netherlands, Sweden, Austria, and Chile. — Deadline: May 15, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Portfolio review fellowship.

item.title: Encontros da Imagem Photobook Award 2026 · Encontros da Imagem
item.description: Photobook award from the 36th edition of Encontros da Imagem festival in Braga, Portugal. Two categories: Best Published Award and Best Dummy Award, each with €1,000 cash prize. Up to two honorable mentions per category. All submitted books shown in a group exhibition during the festival, September 18 – November 1, 2026. Theme: Territory and Identity. Open to artists, photographers and publishers worldwide aged 18+, individually or collectively. Maximum 3 photobooks per applicant per category (each counted as separate entry). Physical books must arrive in Braga by 15 July 2026. — Deadline: May 24, 2026. Fee: €25. Prize: €1,000 (each category) + group exhibition.

item.title: Open Panoràmic 2026 — Burning with Desire · Festival Panoràmic
item.description: Open call from Festival Panoràmic (10th anniversary edition) in Granollers, Barcelona and Terrassa. Theme Burning with Desire takes the bicentennial of photography as its starting point, positioning photography and cinema as practices of desire — for memory, justice, beauty, permanence. Three categories: still image (series or single works), audiovisual essay (5-18 min .mov/.mp4), and installation/other formats. Selected projects included in the festival's exhibition programme, October 15 – December 27, 2026. Open to artists and collectives of any nationality, 18+, individually or collectively. Projects must be created between 2022 and 2026. One project per category maximum. — Deadline: May 25, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Solstice Magazine Issue 72 — Editorial Submissions
item.description: Submit fashion and editorial photography for publication in Issue 72 of Solstice Magazine, a London-based fashion publication. First-round deadline May 18; second-round June 18 if space remains. Issue release June 21, 2026. Editorials must be unpublished. Send via PDF, Dropbox, or WeTransfer. — Deadline: May 18, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Publication.

item.title: Alt+1000 9th Edition Open Call — Emerging Scene
item.description: 9th edition open call from the Alt+1000 outdoor photography festival in La Vue-des-Alpes, canton de Neuchâtel. Theme explores the notion of jeu (play) in connection with landscape — including in-game photography, screen capture, photomontage, and the visual exploration of digital environments and playscapes. Festival runs September 18 to October 10, 2027. Four emerging photographers are selected, each receiving a CHF 800 honorarium with all production, installation, and promotion covered by Alt+1000. Open to photographers and artists using photography who are studying at a Swiss art school or in early career (maximum 5 years after graduating) in Switzerland. All photographic genres and techniques welcome — artistic, conceptual, or documentary. Capacity to adapt to outdoor exhibition is a primary evaluation criterion; proposals requiring electrical power are not accepted. Submission via email as a single .zip with the subject line APPEL À PROJET ALT+1000 2027. Working languages: French and English. — Deadline: May 31, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: CHF 800 + production + outdoor festival exhibition.

item.title: PhEST Pop-Up Open Call 2026 — What If?
item.description: Sixth international contest from PhEST – See Beyond the Sea, the international photography and contemporary art festival in Monopoli, Italy. Theme: WHAT IF? — exploring our relationship with the present and imagining possible futures through visual art. Two categories: SERIES (10–20 fixed images, illustrations) and SINGLES (video, animation, and this year also short films). Six winning projects selected: an exhibition at PhEST 2026 for the best international project, an exhibition for the best Puglia-based artist, an exhibition of the best international short film (UniBa Award), a Fujifilm X-T5 mirrorless camera kit with 16-80mm lens (€2,550 value, offered by Fujifilm Italia), publication on the PhMuseum platform with a free Annual copy, publication on LensCulture, and projection of works during the opening nights of PhEST 2026. Festival runs August 7 – November 1, 2026 in Monopoli, Italy. Submissions via LensCulture (free account required); 200-word English description, short bio, 2000-pixel JPGs. — Deadline: May 13, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Exhibition + Fujifilm camera.

item.title: Ian Parry Photojournalism Grant 2026
item.description: Photojournalism grant honoring Ian Parry, who died at 24 covering the Romanian Revolution in 1989 for The Sunday Times. Open to photographers aged 24 or under, or any age with proof of full-time enrollment in a photographic course. Winner receives £10,000, a year-long mentorship with photojournalist Giles Duley, Canon equipment loans for one year, publication in The Guardian, inclusion in the Hamburg Portfolio Review, and potential safety equipment/hostile environment training via the Gentex Corp award. Partners include Canon, The Guardian, and Legacy of War Foundation. Patron: Sir Don McCullin. Founded over four decades ago. — Deadline: August 31, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: £10,000 + mentorship.

item.title: Seen / Unseen · Decagon Gallery
item.description: Photography exhibition exploring the visible and the implied — works that engage with what is shown, suggested, or hidden. Online curated exhibition with published catalog, social media and newsletter promotion, certificate of participation, and digital badge. First place receives a solo webpage exhibition. Open to photographers worldwide aged 18+. $1,000 total cash awards. — Deadline: July 8, 2026. Fee: $25. Prize: $1,000 total.

item.title: Manifest Season 23 Photo-Solo Exhibit Proposals
item.description: Open call for solo exhibition proposals at Manifest Creative Research Gallery during the 2026/27 season, coinciding with the FotoFocus Biennial in Cincinnati. Approximately one-third of seasonal programming is dedicated to solo exhibitions of original lens-based work. Each exhibiting artist receives a $100 honorarium plus a $1,000 Grand Jury Award for one jury-selected work. Open internationally to artists working in traditional or non-traditional photographic media. — Deadline: June 1, 2026. Fee: $50. Prize: $100 honorarium + $1,000 Grand Jury.

item.title: Yaddo Residency — Summer 2026 Cycle
item.description: Two-week to two-month residency at Yaddo's 400-acre estate in Saratoga Springs, NY, founded in 1900. Open to professional and emerging artists across literature, visual art (painting, drawing, sculpture, printmaking, photography, mixed media, installation), music composition, performance, and film & video. Residents receive room, board, and a private studio; modest access grants available to offset travel. The Summer cycle covers residencies November 2026 through June 2027. Portal opens June 1; application fee waivable in cases of financial hardship. Yaddo encourages applications from artists from backgrounds underrepresented in arts and culture. — Deadline: July 1, 2026. Fee: $35. Prize: Residency.

item.title: E·CO/26 — About Time · VIST Foundation
item.description: Joint open call from VIST Foundation, AECID (Spanish Agency for International Development Cooperation), and NEWF, supporting collective visual projects from Latin America and Africa. Theme: About Time — exploring the relationship between past, present, and future, with attention to ancestral knowledge, memory, territorial connections, and future imaginaries. Twelve collective projects will be selected (six from each region), each receiving a €5,000 production grant. Open to existing or newly-formed groups of three or more people; international projects spanning multiple countries are welcome. Visual, audiovisual, and transmedia formats accepted. Selected groups join a collective production process with virtual mentorship from specialists; final works are presented through travelling exhibitions and the digital platforms of VIST Foundation, NEWF, AECID, and Spanish Cultural Centers. Collective meeting in November 2026 in South Africa. — Deadline: May 10, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: €5,000 production grant × 12 collectives.

item.title: 2026 Book Awards
item.description: Three photobook awards: Author's Book Award (subjective artistic practice), Historical Book Award (documentation/archive), and Photo-Text Book Award (text-image relationship, supported by Fondation Jan Michalski). Each category €6,000. Books must have been published between May 13, 2025 and May 13, 2026. Self-published books without ISBN are eligible; reissues allowed if the first print run was under 150 copies. Shortlisted and winning works are exhibited at Rencontres d'Arles (July 6 – October 4, 2026) and at Jimei x Arles in Xiamen, China. — Deadline: May 13, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: €6,000 × 3 categories.

item.title: Monochromatic Awards 2026 · Dodho Magazine
item.description: Fifth edition of the Dodho Monochromatic Awards, celebrating monochromatic photography in all interpretations — traditional black and white, grayscale, sepia, cyanotype, or any single-tone variation. Jury looks for clear vision, defined intention, and strong execution. Winners and finalists are featured in the Monochromatic Awards 2026 annual printed book (30×30 cm, premium matte paper). The top winner receives 'Photographer of the Year' recognition. Three category prizes plus two honorable mentions receive certificates and editorial visibility. Open globally, individuals or collectives. — Deadline: July 15, 2026. Fee: €30 (3) / €45 (6) / €60 (12). Prize: Photographer of the Year + annual book inclusion.

item.title: Passage Art-Residency-Programme 2026 · Polygona Kunstverein / KOBRA
item.description: Four-week artist-in-residence programme in the Wittenberg region of Saxony-Anhalt, Germany, dedicated to photography and film. Two themed residencies for October 2026: Topic 1 at Ferropolis (the historic Zschornewitz coal-fired power station — energy production, post-industrial landscapes); Topic 2 at the Reformationsgeschichtliche Forschungsbibliothek Wittenberg (a Reformation-era research library — knowledge, visual representation). €5,000 grant per residency, plus €1,000 supplement for artists with children. On-site accommodation, research support, and curatorial guidance provided. Open to national and international artists aged 18+; students not eligible. Notification of results from 20 June 2026. — Deadline: May 30, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: €5,000 grant + accommodation.

item.title: CCI + WOPHA Fellowship 2026 · Pérez Art Museum Miami
item.description: Joint fellowship from PAMM's Caribbean Cultural Institute (CCI) and Women Photographers International Archive (WOPHA), for emerging and mid-career women and non-binary photographers from the Caribbean and its diaspora. Hybrid program runs September–November 2026, with an in-person residency at El Espacio 23 in Miami during September. Fellow receives a stipend, production funds up to $4,000, and round-trip airfare to Miami if not currently based there. Photographic practice broadly defined to include cameraless, computational, and augmented processes, as well as image archiving and circulation. Includes mentorship, curatorial resources, and engagement with the academic community at FIU-LACC. — Deadline: June 1, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Stipend + $4,000 production.

item.title: Camille Lepage Award 2026
item.description: Annual €8,000 award supporting a photojournalist committed to a long-term reporting project. Established by the family of Camille Lepage, the photojournalist killed while reporting in the Central African Republic in 2014. Funded for the tenth year by the SAIF (Société des Auteurs des Arts Visuels et de l'Image Fixe). The award helps a photographer carry out and complete a reporting project already under way. Open to professional photojournalists with no restriction on age, gender, or nationality. Award presented in September 2026 at the International Festival of Photojournalism Visa pour l'Image-Perpignan. The winning report must be completed within one year so that it can be presented at the 2027 festival as an exhibition or evening show. — Deadline: May 4, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: €8,000.

item.title: CIAR Fall Artists' Residency 2026 · Cuttyhunk Island Artists' Residency
item.description: Eight-day residency on Cuttyhunk Island off the Massachusetts coast, September 9–16, 2026. Open to visual artists at all career stages working across drawing, painting, collage, small sculpture, photography, and video. Artists must have a portable studio practice suitable for the island setting. Programming includes communal meals prepared by resident chefs, complimentary golf carts to roam the island, and conversations with visiting artists Claudia Keep and Randall Exon. Housing at the historic Avalon Inn (linens and towels provided); base cost $1,950 (triple) to $3,600 (single) plus ferry travel. Multiple full and partial fellowships available — the new Environmental Artist Fellowship, the Open Merit Fellowship, the Paul Cuffe Fellowship for an artist of color, the Wellspring Fellowship for parent artists, and work-study options — covering up to the full residency cost. — Deadline: May 15, 2026. Fee: $25. Prize: 8-day island residency.

item.title: Urban 2026 · Glasgow Gallery of Photography
item.description: International photography exhibition on the theme of urban environments. Open to street photography that captures the people inhabiting these spaces, cityscapes, architecture, and beyond. Selected work displayed in a month-long gallery exhibition in Glasgow (4–30 September 2026), with work also appearing in an online gallery and exhibition catalogue. All participants put forward for Photographer of the Month consideration. Images printed on Fujifilm photographic paper and framed in gallery frames; photographers retain all copyright. Open to emerging and established photographers, professional and amateur, Scottish and international. Submit 1–8 JPEGs (300ppi minimum, 3000 pixels on shortest side) via free file-transfer to the gallery email. — Deadline: May 22, 2026. Fee: Free (£48 if accepted). Prize: Exhibition + publication.

item.title: Pink 2026 · Glasgow Gallery of Photography
item.description: International photography exhibition exploring the colour pink across any genre — nature, urban settings, portraits, still life, or beyond. Selected work displayed in a month-long gallery exhibition in Glasgow (4–30 September 2026), with work also appearing in an online gallery and exhibition catalogue. All participants put forward for Photographer of the Month consideration. Images printed on Fujifilm photographic paper and framed in gallery frames; photographers retain all copyright. Open to emerging and established photographers, professional and amateur, Scottish and international. Submit 1–8 JPEGs (300ppi minimum, 3000 pixels on shortest side) via free file-transfer to the gallery email. — Deadline: May 22, 2026. Fee: Free (£48 if accepted). Prize: Exhibition + publication.

item.title: Photometria Awards 2026 — Coming of Age · Photometria International Photography Festival
item.description: Open call for the 18th Photometria International Photography Festival in Ioannina, Greece. Theme: Coming of Age (18+) — exploring the layered and evolving condition of growing up, moments of rupture, and the tension between freedom and responsibility. Sole judge: Alec Soth (Magnum, Guggenheim Fellow). 1st prize: Nikon Z30 Kit with NIKKOR Z DX 12-28mm lens. 2nd and 3rd: signed photo album by Alec Soth. One top-three winner receives a solo exhibition at the next festival. Top 25 photos exhibited in Ioannina during the 18th edition (Sep–Nov 2026) and travel to other cities in Greece. AI-generated images not accepted. Entry: free for 1 photo, €5 for 3 photos. — Deadline: May 31, 2026. Fee: Free / €5. Prize: Nikon Z30 + solo exhibition.

item.title: Solo Exhibition June 2026 · All About Photo
item.description: Monthly featured photographer showcase. Winner receives a full month online solo exhibition (June 1–30, 2026), permanent gallery presence, exclusive interview, social media promotion, newsletter feature, international press coverage, and commission-free sales. Submit a cohesive project or portfolio of 6–14 images. — Deadline: May 19, 2026. Fee: $45. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Watershed
item.description: Themed juried exhibition exploring water as subject, symbol, tool, and essential aspect of life. Juried by Luther Smith, photographic artist and Emeritus Professor of Art Photography at Texas Christian University, with work in the Amon Carter Museum, Library of Congress, Dallas Museum of Art, and other major institutions. Exhibition at Pool Gallery, Fort Worth, July 3–25, 2026, with closing reception July 25. $400 first place, $250 second, $150 third, plus up to 5 honorable mentions. Open internationally to all skill levels. — Deadline: June 1, 2026. Fee: $30–$40 / 5 images. Prize: $400 first, $250 second, $150 third.

item.title: Vicinity 2026: What's Going On? · Perspective Gallery
item.description: 9th Annual Juried Exhibition. Inspired by Marvin Gaye's 1971 album exploring social conflict, the show invites artists to respond to 'What's going on?' through inner landscapes or broader human conditions — social, cultural, environmental. Juried by Jan Tichy, professor at the School of the Art Institute of Chicago in Photography and Art & Technology/Sound Practices, with work in MoMA and Israel Museum collections. Open only to photographers based in the Chicago area able to deliver work in person. Exhibition July 2–26, 2026 at Perspective Gallery, Evanston, IL. — Deadline: May 15, 2026. Fee: $35 / 5 images. Prize: $200 Juror's Award + $150 + $100.

item.title: see-zeen Issue 20 Open Call
item.description: Independent online magazine curating contemporary photography by international emerging artists, based in NYC and Berlin. Open theme — any style, genre, or approach (portraiture, landscape, documentary, fashion, abstraction, experimental, conceptual, hybrid). Selected work published on website and social media; unpublished submissions still considered for Instagram. Submit a project statement (max 300 words), work description (max 100 words), bio with contact, and website/Instagram links. — Deadline: May 27, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Publication.

item.title: Photo Trouvée Magazine Issue 20 — Print Call
item.description: Print Issue 20 open call for artists who work with or are inspired by vintage found or family photographs. Any media accepted. Selected artists receive a designated page spread with artist statement, complimentary digital issue, 15% discount code for the print magazine, plus website, newsletter, and social media listings reaching 23.2K+ people. No theme. International submissions welcome. — Deadline: June 15, 2026. Fee: Free to submit; $40 if selected. Prize: Publication (print).

item.title: The House & Garden Show · Blue Sky Gallery
item.description: Online exhibition exploring shelter and nature through intimate interiors, domestic moments, wild backyards, and cultivated landscapes. Literal, abstract, or imaginary interpretations welcome. Part of Blue Sky Gallery's 50th anniversary celebration featuring 12 monthly themed online exhibitions. No membership required. Juried by a special committee. Virtual exhibition launches June 4, 2026. — Deadline: May 15, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Online exhibition.

item.title: Pamplemousse Magazine Issue 13
item.description: Issue 13 of Pamplemousse Magazine, an independent contemporary film photography print magazine based in San Francisco. This call invites artists to respond to provided curated vernacular photographs — exploring the intersection of snapshot and fine art photography. Only original film photography (35mm, 120, large format, polaroid, or alt-process) created in response to one of the provided found photos is accepted. A project statement of 100–300 words is required. Files named FIRSTNAME_LASTNAME_01. — Deadline: May 17, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Publication (print).

item.title: The Life of Color · Praxis Photo Arts Center
item.description: International juried photography exhibition at Praxis Gallery in Minneapolis exploring how color operates as signal — amplifying, unifying, or destabilizing what is seen. Photographers encouraged to use hue, saturation, and value deliberately to construct meaning. Up to 38 photographs selected. Awards include Directors' Choice (free entry to two future calls) and five honorable mentions. Members and artists experiencing financial hardship receive discounted or free entries. Exhibition June 20 – July 11, 2026. — Deadline: May 17, 2026. Fee: $35 for 5 images. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: imagined · A Smith Gallery
item.description: Online juried exhibition exploring the imaginative — visionary, poetic, fanciful, dreamlike, fictional. Juror Susan Burnstine, an award-winning fine art photographer known for creating homemade cameras and lenses. Up to 47 images selected. Awards: Juror's Award (solo online exhibition, hardbound book, blog feature), Director's Award (hardbound book and blog feature), Visitor's Award ($100 for most Instagram likes). Exhibition June 19 – July 30, 2026. Photographers submitting 13+ images receive a complimentary 30-minute portfolio review. — Deadline: May 25, 2026. Fee: $40. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: ABANDONED Photography Exhibit · Dusk Gallery
item.description: Exploring traces of human presence and absence — forgotten structures, deserted landscapes, personal relics, and emotional remnants. 26 selected images exhibited at Dusk Gallery in Santa Fe, NM, July 3–31, 2026. Selected artists receive complimentary professional printing on Luster paper and 24×24 black museum-quality framing. 50% commission on sales. Open worldwide to amateur and professional photographers. — Deadline: May 22, 2026. Fee: $40–$45. Prize: Exhibition + free printing & framing.

item.title: 10th Singapore International Photography Festival 2026 Open Call
item.description: 10th biennial SIPF Open Call for image-makers and photographers worldwide, with no theme. Two categories: Portfolio (cohesive body of work in images and/or video) and Photobook (both published and dummy books, which must be production-ready in physical form). Shortlisted submissions presented in the SIPF Open Call Showcase at the 10th biennale edition of SIPF in Singapore, mid-October to end-November 2026. Three SGD $2,000 cash prizes awarded: Best Portfolio, Best Published Photobook, Best Dummy Photobook. Shortlisted artists receive exposure to SIPF's network, discounted portfolio reviews and masterclasses, complimentary festival admission, and opportunities to participate in artist tours, talks, and workshops. Organised by DECK Photography Art Centre, a registered Charity in Singapore supported by the National Arts Council. Submission fee: USD $30 for Photobook, USD $45 for Portfolio. — Deadline: May 17, 2026. Fee: $30–$45. Prize: 3× SGD $2,000.
